transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-12
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Acme - Head of ML), Samantha Ortiz (Acme - Security Lead), Daniel Park (Acme - Platform Engineer)

Summary:
Quick security/compliance review focused on data residency and region pinning. Acme needs EU-only processing for a subset of tenants, wants clarity on cross-border processing (US fallback), sub-processor list, and KMS/BYOK options. Redwood explained hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment options and audit/logging capabilities. Next steps agreed: share certs, design docs, and schedule BYOK deep-dive.

Topics:
- Region pinning / per-tenant pinning
- Cross-border processing and legal controls (SCCs/DPA)
- Sub-processors and cloud providers
- Encryption and KMS / BYOK
- Audit logs, access controls, RBAC, SSO

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um just to quickly intro my name is Alex Martinez, I'm the AE on the account, Priya from SE will run through the technicals. Quick note recording's on.
[00:15] Priya: Hi all, yeah quick agenda: confirm Acme constraints around EU residency, show how region pinning works today, options if you need absolute EEA-only processing, and BYOK/KMS integration notes.
[00:30] Jordan: Thanks, yeah we have regulatory requirement for certain customers to keep all processing in EU and not have any tokenized payload leave region. So we need region pinning at tenant level, and very clear auditing.
[00:48] Samantha: Also we need the sub-processor list and assurance around cross-border transfers — our legal team asked about SCCs or other transfer mechanisms.
[00:58] Priya: Understood. At a high level, Redwood supports three deployment modes that are relevant: Hosted with region pinning (we run the control plane, you can pin data to a region), Dedicated (reserved capacity in a region with tenant isolation), and Private (VPC or on-prem for full control). For strict EU-only we usually recommend Dedicated in EU or Private.
[01:20] Daniel: If we do hosted with region pinning, is there any scenario where data would cross to US for processing? We can't have user prompts or model context leaving EEA for those tenants.
[01:34] Priya: Good question. Hosted region pinning routes requests to inference pools that are pinned to the region. For most cases data is processed entirely in-region. However there are rare fallback scenarios — e.g., regional capacity exhaustion or emergency failover — where requests may be routed to a compatible model in another region unless you opt into only-in-region SLA.
[01:56] Alex: We can configure strict region enforcement as part of a Dedicated or Private contract; for Hosted we can add language and triggers to avoid cross-region fallback, but that can impact availability during outages. We'll spell out tradeoffs.
[02:12] Jordan: Ok, legal will want the fallback behavior documented. Also curious about sub-processors — e.g., which cloud providers and logging vendors you use?
[02:22] Priya: Our primary cloud regions are GCP and AWS depending on customer region; we can share the sub-processor list. For Hosted, telemetry and metrics are stored in our observability backend, which we can restrict by region for EU customers. Audit logs and request traces can be stored with configurable retention in EU only for pinned tenants.
[02:40] Samantha: On KMS — can you support BYOK so that Acme retains key control? And what about HSM?
[02:48] Priya: Yes, Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations. For Hosted we support BYOK with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and external HSM providers — keys never leave customer control, we do envelope encryption and services only receive encrypted model context. For Private deployments BYOK/HSM is supported as well. There is some engineering work to wire up the rotation and envelope config which we can scope in the pilot.
[03:12] Daniel: How granular are the audit logs? We need per-request identifiers and token-level cost/latency breakdowns for SRE and compliance.
[03:22] Priya: We provide per-request traces, token counts, latency, model version, route, and tenant id. Logs can be exported to your SIEM via log streaming (TLS) or pushed to an S3/GCS bucket in-region. There's an immutable append-only audit trail option for compliance.
[03:45] Jordan: Great. On the legal side, SCCs vs adequacy — what's Redwood using for US transfers?
[03:52] Alex: We provide the DPA and we rely on the standard contractual clauses and whatever current transfer frameworks are appropriate; we'll share the DPA and sub-processor list for your legal to review. We also support contractual commitments to keep processing in-region for Dedicated/Private.
[04:08] Samantha: We need to confirm deletion and retention behavior. For EU tenants we want short retention and assured deletion.
[04:16] Priya: We support per-tenant retention policies for request logs and cached prefixes. For models we have configurable KV cache TTLs and you can opt out of prefix caching for regulated tenants. Deletion requests can be elevated and we'll provide confirmation.
[04:34] Daniel: There's also concern about third-party model weights and the possibility of telemetry or hidden tokens. Do you run third-party inference or only models we onboard?
[04:44] Priya: Both. Redwood can serve curated open models from our catalog, but for regulated customers we recommend pinning to a customer-approved model release and pinning execution to a Dedicated/Private pool. We'll also provide a model provenance manifest and checksum.
[05:02] Jordan: Can you outline the region pinning config? Is it per-tenant tag or per-route?
[05:10] Priya: It's flexible. You can pin at the tenant level or per-route. Typical setup: tenant metadata includes data residency flag (EU-only), the routing policy maps tenant->EU inference pool, and the control plane enforces the policy. We'll share sample config. Note: if a request is for a long context and requires shard / kv cache rehydration, all that happens in-region if pinned.
[05:36] Samantha: What about cross-border analytics? We have BI pipelines that may aggregate latencies across regions — is telemetry anonymized?
[05:45] Priya: Telemetry can be configured to strip PII and only send aggregated metrics cross-region; raw traces for pinned tenants can be retained in-region only.
[05:54] Jordan: Any SLA or contractual language about no data export from EU?
[06:00] Alex: We can include strict processing location commitments in Dedicated/Private SLAs. For Hosted we can put strong contractual reps and controls and offer a high-availability plan within-region. We'll have legal and security craft the exact DPA wording.
[06:12] Daniel: On the KMS flow — can you walk through a short lifecycle?
[06:18] Priya: Sure, simplified: 1) Customer configures their KMS key and grants Redwood service principal limited decrypt/encrypt privileges; 2) Client-side or control-plane envelope encryption wraps model payloads; 3) Redwood runtime holds only encrypted blobs and performs decryption in a secure enclave or trusted node in-region, using ephemeral keys; 4) logs reflect which key id was used but not the plaintext. There is integration work for rotation and key revocation flows.
[06:50] Jordan: Sounds good, but we need proof points for SOC2 controls around key management and access reviews.
[06:56] Alex: We'll send SOC2 and ISO certs and a summary of controls mapping; we also do pen tests and can share redacted reports under NDA.
[07:05] Samantha: Regarding sub-processors — do you use any third-party inference accelerators or model-hosting partners that might be US-located?
[07:14] Priya: We use specific GPU providers and may use partner inference nodes for edge regions; all partners are disclosed as sub-processors and can be contractually limited for EU-only customers. We'll include the list and whether any subprocessors process data outside EU.
[07:30] Daniel: For failover, can you keep requests pending and retry only within region? We need to avoid synchronous cross-border processing even under heavy load.
[07:39] Priya: There are several knobs: strict region-only mode (reject if no capacity), delayed async queueing in-region, or allow cross-region fallback. Each has availability vs compliance tradeoffs. We'll document and you can select default behavior per-tenant.
[07:58] Jordan: For the pilot we'll probably want EU-only and Dedicated to avoid surprises. What does lead time look like?
[08:05] Alex: Dedicated pools in EU have a typical lead time of 2–4 weeks depending on capacity and size; Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) are longer. We'll provide sizing and cost estimates once we have expected traffic.
[08:18] Samantha: About RBAC and SSO: we want SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and granular RBAC for engineers vs security. Can you integrate with our IdP?
[08:27] Priya: Yes we support SAML SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and role-based permissions. Audit events for admin actions are captured and can be exported.
[08:37] Daniel: Any concerns about model caching leaking data across tenants?
[08:42] Priya: We partition caches by tenant id in Dedicated/Private and we have cache-namespace enforcement in Hosted for pinned tenants. For very sensitive tenants we recommend disabling prefix cache.
[08:56] Jordan: Legal asked about breach notification timelines and forensic logs.
[09:02] Alex: Standard is 72 hours for notification, and we can provide forensic logs and retain snapshots for a defined period. We'll include specifics in the DPA.
[09:12] Samantha: Can we get a sample data processing addendum?
[09:16] Alex: Yes, we'll share the DPA and the sub-processor list after this call (action item).
[09:22] Priya: I'll drop the region pinning design doc and config examples. We have a sample terraform snippet for routing policies too.
[09:30] Jordan: One last question — are there any performance implications for EU-only pools?
[09:36] Priya: Latency is slightly improved if pool is in-region; cost/throughput are comparable. The main impact is reduced failover options which can affect availability during regional outages. We'll show historical perf profiles for EU pools.
[09:52] Daniel: Sounds fine. next steps?
[09:55] Alex: Recap: we'll send certs, DPA, sub-processor list, region-pin doc, and schedule BYOK deep-dive. Customer to send tenant list and compliance contacts.
[10:08] Jordan: Thanks, that's helpful. We'll review and get back.
[10:12] Samantha: Thanks everyone.
[10:15] Alex: Thanks all, talk soon.

End of transcript.
